categories.main_business_segments: Kyudenko Corporation (to be renamed KRAFTIA CORPORATION) operates primarily in the facility construction industry, focusing on electrical construction (distribution line, indoor wiring, and telecommunications) and HVAC/plumbing (air conditioning, heating, water supply, sanitation, and water treatment) design and installation. The company also engages in related businesses such as materials and equipment sales, real estate, software development, staffing, renewable energy power generation, environmental analysis, medical support, printing, hotel and golf course management, and commercial facility operations.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages advanced construction and engineering technologies, including ICT/IT tools (cloud mobile cameras, 3D laser scanners, digital twins), heat and airflow simulations, 3D-CAD/BIM, and AI-based HVAC optimization. It conducts R&D in collaboration with universities, focusing on automation (swarm robots for illuminance measurement), drone/satellite/AI-based resource analysis, and energy-efficient building systems. The company also develops proprietary construction methods and tools to enhance safety, quality, and efficiency.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Kyudenko's main customers are utility companies (notably Kyushu Electric Power and its affiliates), public sector entities, and private corporations involved in urban redevelopment, semiconductor plants, logistics facilities, and large-scale infrastructure. The company also serves general private sector clients through its real estate, renewable energy, and facility management businesses.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company operates primarily in Japan, with a strong presence in Kyushu, Kanto, and Kansai regions, and has expanded its business to other parts of Japan and overseas, including subsidiaries in Singapore, Taiwan, Vietnam, Malaysia, and Thailand. Over 90% of sales are generated in Japan, but international operations are growing, particularly in Southeast Asia.
categories.supply_chain_position: Kyudenko is positioned as a downstream player, acting as a general contractor and system integrator in the facility construction and engineering value chain. It also engages in downstream activities such as maintenance, operation, and asset management, while procuring materials and equipment from suppliers and subcontracting some work to group companies.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus is on sustainable growth through technological innovation, digital transformation (DX), productivity improvement, and expansion into new business areas such as renewable energy and stock-based businesses. R&D priorities include automation, AI-driven energy management, smart building systems, and resource efficiency. The company emphasizes human capital development, diversity, and ESG/SDGs alignment as part of its long-term vision.
categories.revenue_model: Kyudenko generates revenue primarily through project-based construction contracts (design and build), ongoing maintenance and facility management services, sales of materials and equipment, real estate sales and leasing, and renewable energy power generation (including FIT/FIP and corporate PPA schemes). Additional income streams include software development, staffing, and various service businesses.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Kyudenko is one of Japan’s leading facility construction and engineering companies, ranking among the top 'subcontractors' (subcons) in both electrical and HVAC/plumbing segments. Major competitors include other large general contractors and specialized facility engineering firms. The company is recognized for its strong market share in Kyushu and growing presence in Kanto and Kansai, with a reputation for technical excellence and reliability.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: For the fiscal year ending March 2025, consolidated net sales were ¥473.9 billion, with operating profit of ¥41.4 billion and net profit attributable to parent shareholders of ¥28.9 billion. The company has over 10,800 employees and maintains a solid balance sheet with high equity ratio (63.5%). Sales and profits have shown steady growth, with record-high results in recent years and a positive outlook for continued expansion.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Kyudenko differentiates itself through comprehensive engineering capabilities, high-quality and reliable project delivery, advanced use of digital and automation technologies, and a strong commitment to sustainability and customer value creation. Its integrated approach, technical expertise, and focus on innovation and ESG allow it to offer tailored solutions for complex infrastructure and energy projects, supporting clients’ needs for efficiency, safety, and environmental performance.
